title: GRT business plan and rural school speed limits
subtitle: Also: Duke Street and Speedsville Road assumptions, asset management service levels, airport economic study, and delegations on speed cameras.
overview: The committee received the Grand River Transit (GRT) business plan for information and recommended a special meeting on April 16 to hear public input {{vote:m5}}. An amendment {{vote:m4}} directs staff to bring the final plan back to the committee for a decision after meeting with interested area municipalities, so the decision will come later than first planned.

On rural school zones, the committee recommended lowering the speed limit near two rural schools, on Lobsinger Line and Northfield Drive, from 40 km/h to 60 km/h {{vote:m7}}. It also directed staff to look at flashing lights alongside speed cameras {{vote:m8}} and to work with township staff on a rural speed zone strategy {{vote:m9}}. Staff said they would report back on the safety implications.

The committee also recommended that Council take over Duke Street West in Kitchener {{vote:m2}} and Speedsville Road in Cambridge {{vote:m3}} as Regional roads, and endorse levels of service for Regional assets {{vote:m6}}. It heard a study on the airport's economic impact and delegations on speed cameras, a Kitchener intersection and GRT day passes. Staff will report back on the intersection and day passes. The committee then met in closed session on a legal matter.

decisions.detail: The committee received the plan for information and recommended a special committee meeting on April 16, 2025 to hear public input, with staff to bring back a final version for a decision.
The committee recommended that staff meet with all interested area municipalities before presenting the final GRT Business Plan to the committee for a decision.
The committee recommended preparing by-laws to lower school zone limits from 40 km/h to 60 km/h on Lobsinger Line near King Alfred Academy and Northfield Drive near Balsam Grove Parochial School.
The committee directed staff to investigate flashing lights that operate during school hours alongside active speed cameras, as part of the rural strategy.
The committee directed staff to work with township staff to create a rural speed zone strategy.

The committee recommended adding Duke Street West between Victoria Street North and Breithaupt Street in Kitchener to the Regional road network, with no parking at all times and no stopping 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. on weekdays.
The committee recommended that Speedsville Road in Cambridge become Regional Road 82, with a 60 km/h speed limit, a no heavy trucks designation and a pedestrian crossover.
The committee recommended that Council endorse the levels of service in Appendix A of report EES-SAM-25-001.

debate: Delegates from the Lobsinger Line area opposed the 40 km/h school zone and speed camera. They said drivers were passing aggressively and tailgating compliant drivers, the school is private with drop-off in its parking lot, and a community petition showed strong opposition. They asked for flashing lights during school hours and a higher limit.

Staff said the 40 km/h limit rests on pedestrian survival odds, which fall sharply at 60 km/h. They said drivers had been recorded far above the limit since the cameras began capturing speeds, and the extra travel time through the zone is small. They suggested road design as an alternative and asked to report back. Several councillors said rural through-roads differ from town streets and that flashing lights suit them.

On the GRT plan, Cambridge councillors pressed for priority on rapid transit and rail links, given their city's long contribution to the LRT through area rating. Staff said the plan is scalable and each year's expansion would be set through budget. Township councillors stressed that area-rated costs fall on township taxpayers.

The amendment to meet area municipalities split the committee. Supporters said elected officials of area councils had only just seen the full plan and that area-rated costs affect their taxpayers. Opponents said engagement ran for nearly a year, staff had worked with municipal staff, and transit is a Regional decision. Staff said a delay to a later meeting was workable.

On Duke Street, a councillor asked that public art, lighting and sound in the new underpass be addressed from the start. Staff said talks were under way with the City of Kitchener and Metrolinx. On Speedsville Road, a councillor raised that the report gave no capital costs. Staff said these would come through the capital budget.
